Regarding precepts: this mind is sufficient to accord with the fundamental intention of all Buddhas and sufficient to harmonize with the original vows of all Bodhisattvas.

Therefore, within a single thought-moment, one immediately receives the empowerment of the Buddhas of the ten directions, the protection and sustenance of all Bodhisattvas, the guardianship of the eight classes of devas and nagas, and the reverent admiration of all spirits and deities.
Because by once generating the Great Mind (*mahācitta*), one receives a slight benefit from the precepts; ultimately, one will certainly attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
Even if past karma has not been extinguished, or if one has committed transgressions by violating the precepts, such that one falls into hell, the punishment received will be light.
This is because, above, one receives the grace of empowerment, and below, one relies on the power of veneration; thus, heavy sins can be mitigated, and evil...

The Way can also be swiftly realized. To illustrate this by analogy: suppose there is a son from a humble family living in the countryside who, having suddenly encountered the right conditions, receives a slight measure of the King’s favor and patronage.

In an instant, he acquires great influence, such that all those who have long served in officialdom—the high-ranking officials, the clerks, and the soldiers—must regard him with renewed respect and dare not treat him with contempt or insolence.
If one happens to commit an offense and is detained by the authorities, their heavy crimes will be mitigated and they will be released from prison swiftly;

this is an inevitable consequence of the law. By this, we know that the various ways of generating the resolve for enlightenment and receiving the precepts differ greatly, and the resulting karmic fruits are likewise vastly distinct.
How could these be compared to the precepts of the śrāvakas or those of the human and celestial realms?
Therefore, whether one is ordained or lay, male or female, regardless of noble or humble status, or wise or foolish, all should listen to and receive the Bodhisattva Great Precepts. Even those who,
being enmeshed in worldly entanglements or beset by difficulties, possess heavy obstacles and deep delusions such that they cannot receive and uphold them according to the Dharma,
may still be permitted to accept them according to their capacity, or to joyfully listen to and recite them, thereby establishing the conditions for Prajñā and planting the seeds of Bodhi.
O Disciples of the Tathāgata: the seed of the great mind of Bodhi is stored within the field of the eight consciousnesses;
from birth to birth, it is neither destroyed nor lost. Suddenly, when encountering circumstances and meeting conditions, there will inevitably come a time of its manifestation. Therefore it is said:

"To sit and receive [the precepts] and then break them is still superior to not receiving the precepts at all. It is better to receive them and yet commit transgressions than to not receive them and remain without."
There is transgression; there is one who commits transgressions called a bodhisattva, because there are precepts that can be transgressed, and thus there is no such thing as "non-transgression.

Non-Buddhists have no precepts to transgress; therefore, even when a *campaka* flower has withered, it still surpasses all other flowers. A bhikṣu who has broken the precepts still surpasses non-Buddhists.

This is because non-Buddhists hold wrong views and do not receive the Buddha’s precepts, remaining forever submerged in the evil realms with no prospect of escape. [The bhikṣu], though having broken [the precepts]...

A precept-holding bhikṣu whose great resolve has not been lost will, even if reborn in the evil realms, become the sovereign of those realms; with a single thought of turning the light back within, he immediately attains liberation.
Therefore, the ancient masters said: "Though one breaks the precepts and undergoes retribution, in the end one ascends to the field of liberation."
If one does not receive [the precepts] or violates them, one will fall forever into the suffering of the hells. The *Ratnavyuha Sūtra* (*Yingluo jing*) states:

"If all sentient beings do not receive the Bodhisattva precepts, they cannot be called those possessing consciousness; they are no different from animals and cannot be called human. They are perpetually separated from the ocean of the Triple Gem;

It is like one who attempts to fly without wings or to cross over without a boat; such things cannot be achieved. If one seeks a sublime fruit without pure ethical discipline (*śīla*), it is likewise impossible.
Even if a person abandons this discipline, though they dwell in the mountains practicing austerities, eating fruits, and taking medicinal herbs, [they will not attain the goal].

"You bhikṣus, after my parinirvāṇa, you should honor, treasure, and revere the *Prātimokṣa* as if encountering light in darkness, or as if a poor man finding a treasure. You should know that this is your great teacher;
were I to remain in the world, it would be no different. Thus, our Buddha, the World-Honored One, [regarded] this dharma of the precepts...
Since the earnest exhortations are thus, and the diligent entrustments are likewise so, they may be called truly essential. Alas!
More than two thousand three hundred years have passed since the World-Honored One entered parinirvāṇa. Now is precisely the autumn of the Final Dharma in this world of five turbidities;
the faculties of sentient beings are frivolous and they lack correct knowledge and vision. How much more so when encountering—
When the noble and holy ones have gone into hiding, the false teachings flourish and blaze.

Since the noble and holy ones have already vanished, who then shall uphold the Bodhisattva Great Precepts—the true lineage and gateway of the Buddhas' wisdom-life? Consequently, no one remains to expound them.

As the True Dharma is not being taught by anyone, false teachers are able to act with unrestrained license, preaching false doctrines, practicing false paths, demonstrating false views, and transmitting false interpretations, thereby deluding [sentient beings].
